candidates.reason: Primary owner of the change: this module imports open_in_browser from scrapy.utils.response and is the only test file that exercises it directly. It contains the flaky CPU-time helper _assert_open_in_browser_is_fast (line 216) plus the two adversarial tests that the PR titles as flaky and as using a broken exploit input: test_open_in_browser_redos_comment (line 229, payload b'-><!--\x00' * 250_000 + b'->\n<!---->') and test_open_in_browser_redos_head (line 236, payload b'<head\t' * 80_000). The same module holds the behaviour assertions (base-tag placement, comment preservation, doctype handling, .txt output, TypeError) that must stay green. Running the module is the direct way to reproduce and verify both PR fixes.

Indirect integration surface for the same code path: the scrapy view command calls open_in_browser (scrapy/commands/view.py:28), and TestViewCommand.test_view (line 687) runs that command end to end against the mockserver, then reads the file:// output and asserts the served HTML body is present. It is a secondary candidate rather than the regression target, because it does not cover the ReDoS payloads or the timing helper in tests/test_utils_response.py; use it to confirm that the base-tag injection behaviour of open_in_browser is unchanged after the test rework.
